page: Microsoft Azure F32-8amds_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine from the Famdsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated physical cores and 8 vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The server is equipped with an exceptionally large memory capacity of 256.0 GB, translating to 32.0 GB of RAM per core, making it highly suitable for memory-intensive applications. Additionally, it bundles 3780 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and is Premium Storage capable, though it does not include any GPU accelerators.

Performance benchmarks highlight strong single-core capabilities. The single-core stress-ng CPU performance, single-threaded gzip compression, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression benchmarks all rank in the top tier (top 10%). Multi-core CPU performance, passmark CPU scores, and memory bandwidth (both cached and uncached) fall into the average category. For database and caching workloads, the instance delivers an average of 23.6 million operations per second on Redis SET operations and average performance in Passmark database operations. Large-model LLM inference (70B) is poor, but small-model (135M) text generation reaches top-tier speeds.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the F32-8amds_v7 offers high resource density, combining massive memory and local NVMe storage relative to its 8 vCPUs. This makes it a qualitatively cost-effective choice for workloads that require large datasets to be held in memory or local high-speed storage without paying for unnecessary extra CPU cores. Tradeoffs include average multi-core scaling and poor large-scale LLM inference performance. This server is best suited for memory-intensive databases, caching layers, data processing, and single-threaded execution tasks.
